assessments.reasoning: Line 13 in the pinned Win32 COM translation guide distinguishes features provided by the language from an object model a host may also expose. Its Internet Explorer example supplies a concrete illustration of the distinction.

challenge.method: Compared the host language with the preceding paragraph on built-in behavior, the ADO server example (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/client-developer/access/desktop-database-reference/vbscript-ado-programming), and vendor documentation of Office builds resolving VBScript.RegExp differently (https://devblogs.microsoft.com/microsoft365dev/how-to-prepare-vba-projects-for-vbscript-deprecation/).
challenge.results: Browser, server and Office integrations expose different objects and have distinct version conditions. The document supports the possibility of host-provided objects without guaranteeing a common object model or restricting the behavior of a particular host.

limitations: The claim describes the distinction in Microsoft documentation. It makes no observation of installed host components or inference about available operating-system capabilities.
